newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile rises on report of $75/shr offer.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile rises on report of $75/shr offer.

text.p: Shares of Mercantile Stores Co Inc rose almost 10 percent Friday on a report the department store chain has received a bid from rival Federated Department Stores Inc.
Fairfield, Ohio-based Mercantile reportedly received an offer of $75 a share from Federated and rejected it.

Mercantile, which operates Maison Blanche, J.B. White, McAlpin's and Gayfers stores, was not immediately available to comment on the report in Business Week magazine. The company's shares rose $5-5/8 to $62-3/8.

The 102-store chain has been on the radar screen of several retailers, including Federated, May Department Stores Co and Dillard's Inc for several years, Wall Street analysts said. But Mercantile has not agreed to a marriage either because the offers it received were too low or the Milliken family, which owns 40 percent of the company, could not iron out estate planning issues.

"I think Mercantile could be bought," said Walter Loeb, a retail industry consultant in New York. "Roger Milliken had negotiated with May at one point. But Mercantile wanted a hefty premium over the stock price."
Cincinnati-based Federated, which owns Bloomingdale's and Macy's, said it does not comment on rumors. May Department Stores, parent of Lord & Taylor and Famous-Barr, also would not comment.
Roger Milliken, his brother Gerrish Milliken and cousin Minot Milliken own 40 percent of Mercantile and are members of the company's board.

Three years ago, Mercantile's shares soared when it issued a statement that it was negotiating a possible business combination. May was widely believed to be the suitor, but the talks apparently collapsed on a disagreement over price.
About a month later, Mercantile's shares climbed again, and Dillard was thought to be mulling a bid. But nothing happened.

Some analysts said the Milliken family was unlikely to accept a deal unless it received a rich premium over the stock's existing price to help cover tax liabilities or unless there was a change in the capital gains tax laws.
Minot and Roger Milliken were both 81 and Gerrish was 79 years old at the time of a company filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission last April.
